punchline: A monk in a brain scanner felt burned out when sharing others' pain, but not when he simply wished them well.
thirty_sec: Neuroscientist Tania Singer scanned the monk Matthieu Ricard. During compassion meditation, the circuits for feeling others' pain stayed quiet. When he was asked to share their pain, those circuits lit up and he compared the state to burnout. A training study from the group found empathy training raised negative feeling, and compassion training reversed it. Paul Bloom reads this as: caring lasts longer than absorbing pain.
